 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Sanjay Kumar Singh
Oral Order
3 25-02-2026 1-Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor representing the State.

2-This appeal under Sections 415 (2) and 430 (1) of B.N.S.S., 2023, has been preferred by the appellant namely Sohail Ansari @ Suhail Ansari against the judgment of conviction dated 21.05.2025 and order of sentence dated 24.05.2025 passed by the District and Additional Sessions-IV- cum-Exclusive Special Judge (Rape and POCSO), Sitamarhi, in Sessions Trial No.209 of 2018 (Registration No.209 of 2018), arising out of Parsauni Police Station Case No.10 of 2018 (G.R. No.380 of 2018), District-Sitamarhi, convicting the appellant for the offence under Section 366 of the Indian Penal Code and sentencing him 5 years' simple imprisonment and fine of Rs.
Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.2531 of 2025(3) dt.25-02-2026 10,000/- and in default of payment of fine, six months' additional simple imprisonment.
3-The appellant has prayed for suspension of his sentence and release on bail during the pendency of this Criminal Appeal before this Court.
4-Brief facts of the case, which are required to be stated are that the informant got the First Information Report lodged on 02.02.2018 stating inter alia that on the date of occurrence, i.e.,
24.12.2017 at about 03:00 A.M. she came out of her room to go to bathroom and when she was going towards courtyard, all of sudden, appellant who was present there from before hiding himself caught hold of her and gauged her mouth.

sentences.text: 1 Ansari, the brothers of the appellant, who had hiding themselves in the dark, came near her and pointed the Nalkatua at her right temple.

At that time, accused Raju Ansari asked the informant that she would have to come with them and she would have to perform Nikah with Sohail Ansari (appellant), otherwise they would kill her and her family members.
They also threatened the informant to kill her, if she would raise alarm.
Out of fear, as per their instructions, the informant came out of the house through the room of her washroom and they got the informant boarded on Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.2531 of 2025(3) dt.25-02-2026 the bolero vehicle in which accused Kamruddin Ansari and Sakina Khatoon were sitting from before.
Thereafter, Sakina Khatoon gave biscuit to the informant to eat.

The informant was not eating the same but out of fear,
she ate the same.
After eating the same, the informant started feeling a sense of intoxication and she became unable to speak.
After reaching at Belsand, accused Raju Ansari, Kamruddin Ansari and Sakina Khatoon alighted there.

Thereafter, the appellant and accused Salman Ansari took the informant to Patna, where Salman Ansari placed the informant and the appellant on the Patna Kurla Express and Salman Ansari returned from Patna.
On the way, appellant served the informant food and biscuit and after taking the same, the informant started feeling in a semi unconscious state.
After reaching at Kurla, Rauf Ansari, the maternal uncle of the appellant, took them to his house at Nala Supara Mumbai.
Thereafter, the appellant snatched the gold ornaments of the informant and after causing assault to the informant, at the point of Nalkatua committed rape on her.
5-It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
Impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence of the appellant is not sustainable in the eyes of the law.
It is Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.2531 of 2025(3) dt.25-02-2026 further submitted that initially FIR was lodged against six accused persons for the alleged offence under Sections 366, 367, 368, 376, 323, 379, 506 and 149 of the Indian Penal Code but after culmination of investigation charge sheet was submitted against four persons.
The charges under Sections 366, 367 and 506 of the IPC were framed against Salman Ansari, Raju Ansari and kamruddin Ansari.

So far as appellant Sohail Ansari is concerned, charges under Sections 366, 367, 506, 386, 379 and 376 of the IPC were framed against him but the prosecution could not prove its case so far as alleged offence under Sections 368, 379, and 376 of the IPC is concerned, hence the appellant was acquitted of the aforesaid charges.
The victim was also found major.
The doctor in the medical report has mentioned inter alia
that it is difficult to show that whether rape has occurred or not.

Much emphasis has been given by contending that appellant has been convicted only for the offence under Section 366 IPC for a period of 5 years, out of which appellant has served incarceration period of about 1 year 10 months.
On the strength of aforesaid facts, it is argued that part of the prosecution story has been disbelieved by the Trial Court.
There is no material evidence on record to constitute an offence under Section 366 of IPC against the appellant, as the Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.2531 of 2025(3) dt.25-02-2026 basic ingredients to constitute an offence under Section 366 IPC are lacking in the present case.
Lastly, it is submitted that in case appellant is granted bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in early hearing of this appeal.

6-Learned A.P.P. for the State opposed the prayer for bail by contending that prosecution has proved it's case beyond reasonable doubt, hence at this stage presumption of innocence is not available to the appellant.

sentences.text: 2 7 -Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in it's entirety, I find that appellant has been acquitted for the alleged offence under Sections 368, 379, and 376 of the IPC and he has served one year ten months sentence.
Considering the huge pendency of the cases, there is no likelihood for final hearing of this case before completing the entire sentence.
There is no material on record to presume that there is danger, of course, of justice being thwarted by grant of bail to the appellant.

8-Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and the reasons as mentioned above, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant is liable to be released on bail Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.2531 of 2025(3) dt.25-02-2026 during pendency of this Criminal Appeal.
9-In view of the above, the sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this Criminal Appeal.

10-Let the appellant-Sohail Ansari @ Suhail Ansari be enlarged on bail during pendency of this appeal in above Case on his furnishing bail bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned subject to deposit of 50% amount fine.
The realization of remaining 50% amount of fine shall remain stayed till disposal of this Criminal Appeal.
11-On acceptance of the bail bonds, the concerned Court below shall furnish the photocopy thereof to this Court for being kept on record of this Criminal Appeal.
12-Let this Criminal Appeal be listed in due course for hearing.

(Sanjay Kumar Singh, J) Prakash/-
